gap.description: BA's PATH C explanation focuses on the SURFACE cause (scan_codex_via_fd needs live fd → cgroup-killed process → no fd → not enumerated). But BA's own context_path-dependent_shared_infra includes happy-session-recovery.sh as read-only reference. BA did not investigate the recovery script's restore path (lines 1019-1108) and missed the structural defect: line 1041 only falls back to peak-snapshot when saved-list is FULLY empty. Daemon's own claude-session re-spawn re-populated saved-list with 5 claude tids on restart → restore took the non-empty branch → peak-snapshot fallback skipped → 019dd077 (only in peak) was never read. Combined with the scoped-save path at lines 539-558 that overwrites session_dirs.txt without peak-protection, codex sessions have a single fragile recovery path while claude sessions have a daemon-internal Plan-A respawn fallback.
gap.should_have_been: out_of_scope_observations entry flagging the recovery_script:1041 design gap as a separate concern, so a follow-up cycle (or the close-report) can decide whether to fix it. dimension_objections.summary: BA's PATH C explanation correctly identifies the surface symptom (no live fd → not in scan_codex_via_fd output). The orchestrator's deeper investigation found the deeper structural gap (line 1041 conditional + scoped-save overwrite). dimension_objections.ba_path_c_explanation: scan_codex_via_fd (lines 798-818) requires the codex process to hold an open fd to the rollout — with the cgroup-killed process gone, the fd is closed, so the tid never enters the watcher's enumeration. Manual `recover <uuid>` bypasses this requirement.
dimension_objections.deeper_investigation_finding: Even with the watcher running, the auto-restore path at line 1019-1108 takes the non-empty saved-list branch (because daemon's own claude-session re-spawn re-populates session_dirs.txt with 5 claude tids), so peak-snapshot fallback at line 1041 is skipped, and 019dd077 (only in the peak snapshot) is never iterated.
dimension_objections.consistency_check: Both findings are correct and consistent. BA's explanation is necessary-but-not-sufficient: the watcher CAN see codex tids (via Source 1 history-jsonl, Source 2 snapshots, Source 3 fd-scan, Source 4 codex-rollout-cwd) even without a live fd — BUT those Sources are only consulted in the recover_session SUBCOMMAND, NOT in the auto-restore path (`do_restore` at lines 1019-1108) which only iterates over session_dirs.txt + (if empty) peak-snapshot. So the auto-restore is genuinely broken for cgroup-killed codex sessions when ANY claude session is alive in the same daemon — exactly the scenario at 22:16. BA's surface explanation is correct; the deeper structural reason that the surface symptom matters is the line-1041 design gap.
dimension_objections.caveat: BA stopped at the surface. The user's follow-up '调查为什么codex session没有被自动恢复' (investigate why codex sessions weren't auto-recovered) — if posed before BA wrote the spec — would have required BA to investigate the auto-restore path. BA's current spec answers 'how to recover NOW' but does not answer 'why did auto-recovery skip this session structurally'. The orchestrator's deeper investigation closed that gap. For C2 scope, this caveat is acceptable (recovery action was the asked deliverable, not auto-recovery audit). For close-report and follow-up planning, the deeper finding must be propagated.

objections.objection: BA missed the deeper auto-recovery design defect and did not capture it in out_of_scope_observations.
objections.evidence: BA's spec correctly explains why scan_codex_via_fd (Source 3) couldn't enumerate 019dd077 post-kill. But BA did not investigate the auto-restore path (do_restore at /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1019-1108). QA verified by reading lines 530-558 (scoped save) and 1030-1108 (restore loop): the scoped save at line 555 unconditionally overwrites session_dirs.txt with scan_running_sessions output (no peak-merge). The restore at line 1041 only consults peak-snapshot when saved-list is FULLY empty (`if [ -z "$saved" ]`), not when saved-list is missing entries. Combined effect: when daemon restarts, claude sessions get re-spawned by daemon's own Plan-A loop and re-populate session_dirs.txt with 5 claude tids → saved is non-empty → peak-snapshot fallback skipped → 019dd077 (only in peak) is silently dropped. Codex sessions have only ONE recovery path (the recovery script's auto-restore), so this gap means cgroup-killed codex sessions are permanently unreachable by auto-recovery whenever ANY claude session is alive in the same daemon.
objections.why_low_severity: C2 scope is recovery action for 019dd077, which BA delivered correctly and the user successfully executed. The auto-recovery defect is a separate (structural) concern — fixing it would prevent a recurrence but does not invalidate this cycle's deliverable. C2's user-need ('提供修复方案') is satisfied. The deeper concern is a candidate for a follow-up cycle/spec.

Surface for a follow-up structural-fix cycle.' Severity: low (does not block C2 PASS).
